title: Supply Chain Siege
summary: You are the DevSecOps engineer responding to a compromised release pipeline. Remove the exposed credential, prevent it from returning, replace unsafe dependency installation, and leave an auditable remediation commit.

objectives.title: Contain the exposed credential
objectives.description: Remove .env from both the working tree and the Git index.

objectives.title: Prevent credential regression
objectives.description: Add the exact line .env to .gitignore so local secrets are not recommitted.

objectives.title: Harden the release workflow
objectives.description: Pin checkout to a full commit SHA and replace the pipe-to-shell installer with the repository's reviewed installer.

objectives.title: Record an auditable remediation
objectives.description: Commit all remediation changes and leave the repository clean.

debrief: Secrets must be removed from tracked content and rotated in the real provider; deleting a file alone does not erase earlier Git history.
Mutable action tags can change underneath a pipeline, while a full commit SHA makes the dependency reviewable and reproducible.
Piping network responses directly into a shell crosses a trust boundary without an integrity check.
A clean remediation commit provides evidence that responders and reviewers can audit.
